description: Definition document AND classification spec for the ClaimType enum in backend/contracts.py — kept 1:1 with it. Each value is a LEGAL-ENTITY category naming the body of law that governs the claim. This file is injected into the Stage-3 extractor's prompt (definition + examples steer classification) and read by the Stage-4 checker. normalized_fields is a CONTRACT between extractor and checker: when the extractor emits a Claim of a given type, it guarantees these payload fields (fields marked '?' are present when determinable, else null); claim_plane rule predicates consume exactly these fields. Extractor convention: a text span embodying two legal categories yields two Claim objects (no multi-label).

triggering_term.legal_concept: Reg Z 'triggering terms' — payment amounts, number of payments, repayment periods, downpayments, finance-charge amounts (closed-end) and their open-end analogues incl. negative claims — whose presence obligates companion disclosures
triggering_term.definition: A span stating a SPECIFIC numeric cost-of-credit term: a payment amount, a number of payments or repayment period, a downpayment amount or percentage, or a finance-charge amount. Specificity is the test: a concrete figure or period qualifies; a general or absence-based statement does not. Open-end (card) analogues include negative fee claims ('no annual fee'), which trigger under 1026.16(b) even though absence-based closed-end statements do not.

positive: Repayment in as many as 36 monthly installments

negative.reason: per the official interpretation of 1026.24(d)(1), absence statements like 'no downpayment' do not trigger — the provision applies only if a downpayment is actually required
per the official interpretation, a statement of the APR alone is not a triggering term (it is a rate_or_apr claim instead)

normalized_fields.payment_amount?: number — dollar payment per period, if stated
normalized_fields.num_payments?: integer — number of payments, if stated
normalized_fields.term_months?: integer — repayment period normalized to months, if stated
normalized_fields.downpayment?: number — downpayment amount or percentage, if stated (with downpayment_is_pct flag)
normalized_fields.finance_charge?: number — finance-charge dollar amount, if stated

rate_or_apr.legal_concept: Rate representations: advertised rates must be stated and labeled as an annual percentage rate, with prominence rules for simple rates
rate_or_apr.note: 12 CFR 1026.24(b)-(c); mortgage presentation also 1026.24(f); open-end analogues in 1026.16.
rate_or_apr.definition: A span stating a NUMERIC rate of credit — a percentage figure presented as the cost of borrowing, whether labeled APR, labeled as an interest rate, or unlabeled. Includes floors ('as low as 8.99%') and ranges ('8.99-35.99% APR'). A rate adjective without a figure ('low rates') is not this type; a promotional rate is emitted as promotional_or_introductory AND as rate_or_apr (two claims).

negative.reason: no numeric figure — not a rate statement under 1026.24(b)-(c), and not an APR-labeling issue; classify as general_udaap_representation if it makes a measurable comparative claim, else no claim
a percentage that is not a cost-of-credit rate

normalized_fields.value_pct?: number — the single rate figure, if one value stated
normalized_fields.range_min_pct?: number — low end, if a range is stated
normalized_fields.range_max_pct?: number — high end, if a range is stated
normalized_fields.is_floor_claim: boolean — true for 'as low as'/'from'/'starting at' framing
normalized_fields.labeled_as_apr: boolean — true if the figure carries the APR label
normalized_fields.rate_kind: enum: apr | interest_rate | unlabeled — how the figure is presented (serves the not_conflated comparator)

promotional_or_introductory.legal_concept: Promotional/introductory rate and deferred-interest representations, with adjacency and proximity requirements
promotional_or_introductory.definition: A span offering a temporary rate or interest holiday: an introductory/promotional rate (typically 0% or reduced, for a stated period) or a deferred-interest offer ('no interest if paid in full in N months'). The span qualifies when a rate or interest treatment is presented as time-limited or conditional on payoff; the same figure also yields a rate_or_apr claim.

positive: No interest if paid in full in 12 months

negative.reason: time-limits the OFFER, not a rate — urgency device (general_udaap_representation), not a promotional-rate representation
a conditional discount, not a temporary promotional period — rate_or_apr only

normalized_fields.promo_rate_pct: number — the promotional rate figure (0 for 0%)
normalized_fields.promo_period_months?: integer — promo duration in months, if stated
normalized_fields.is_deferred_interest: boolean — true for 'no interest if paid in full' structures
normalized_fields.post_promo_rate_stated: boolean — the go-to rate (or range) appears in the creative

fixed_rate_representation.legal_concept: 'Fixed' rate representations — permitted only for rates that genuinely cannot increase (or with a stated fixed period); banned for variable/adjustable products
fixed_rate_representation.note: 12 CFR 1026.16(f) (open-end); Reg N 12 CFR 1014.3 and Reg Z 1026.24(i)(1) (mortgage).
fixed_rate_representation.definition: A span applying the word 'fixed' (or an equivalent immutability claim like 'your rate will never change') to a credit product's RATE or payment. The word 'fixed' applied to something other than the rate/payment of the credit product does not qualify.

positive: Fixed 6.25% APR for the life of the loan
Lock in a fixed monthly payment
Your rate will never go up

negative.span: Stay on a fixed monthly budget
negative.reason: 'fixed' modifies the consumer's budget, not the product's rate or payment — not a rate representation

negative.span: We fixed our fee schedule in 2024
negative.reason: 'fixed' as verb about the lender's pricing history, not an immutability claim about the offered rate

normalized_fields.applies_to_rate: boolean — true when 'fixed'/immutability modifies the product's rate or payment
normalized_fields.fixed_period_stated?: string — the stated period during which the rate is fixed, if any (null = unbounded claim)

approval_or_prequalification.legal_concept: Approval and likelihood-of-approval representations: 'pre-approved' gated by the FCRA firm offer of credit; mortgage approval-likelihood misrepresentation banned by Reg N
approval_or_prequalification.note: FCRA 603(l), 15 USC 1681a(l) (firm offer definition); Reg N 12 CFR 1014.3(q). 'Prequalified' has no statutory definition — its boundaries are enforcement doctrine (FTC v. Credit Karma).
approval_or_prequalification.definition: A span representing the consumer's approval status or likelihood of approval: pre-approved/prequalified badges, guarantee-of-approval language, numeric or qualitative approval odds. Process descriptions (how to apply, how fast) are not approval claims unless they assert an outcome.

positive: 90%+ approval odds for members like you

negative.reason: describes the application process, asserts nothing about the outcome — not an approval claim

negative.span: Checking your rate won't affect your credit score
negative.reason: a credit-pull mechanics claim (general_udaap_representation / soft_pull_claim), not an approval representation

normalized_fields.badge_word: string — the operative term as rendered ('pre-approved', 'prequalified', 'guaranteed', ...)
normalized_fields.strength: enum: guaranteed | pre_approved | prequalified | odds_numeric | odds_qualitative | invitation — descending assertiveness of the outcome claim
normalized_fields.odds_value_pct?: number — the numeric odds figure, when strength=odds_numeric

fee_or_cost.legal_concept: Fee and cost-of-credit representations against the TILA finance-charge concept; 'no fees' claims judged under deception doctrine
fee_or_cost.note: TILA/Reg Z 12 CFR 1026.4 (finance charge); Reg N 12 CFR 1014.3(c) (mortgage fee/cost misrepresentation). 'No hidden fees' style claims have no statutory test — anchor is UDAAP/FTC Section 5 net impression.
fee_or_cost.definition: A span representing the presence, absence, or amount of a fee or non-rate cost of the product: 'no hidden fees', '$0 annual fee', 'origination fee of 1-8%', 'no closing costs'. Note the asymmetry: absence-of-fee claims are NOT closed-end triggering terms (per interp-24), but 'no annual fee' IS an open-end trigger — the checker resolves that via CC-TRIG-001; this type just normalizes the fee claim itself.

positive: An origination fee of 1-8% is deducted from proceeds

negative.reason: a payment amount (triggering_term), not a fee representation

negative.span: Save thousands over the life of your loan
negative.reason: a savings outcome claim (general_udaap_representation), not a statement about a fee

normalized_fields.fee_claim_kind: enum: absence_of_fee | specific_fee_amount | fee_disclosure — asserting no fees, stating a fee figure, or disclosing fee mechanics
normalized_fields.fee_type?: enum: annual_fee | origination_fee | closing_costs | balance_transfer_fee | other — which fee, if identifiable
normalized_fields.amount_value?: number — the fee amount or percentage, if stated (with amount_is_pct flag)

endorsement_or_testimonial.legal_concept: Endorsements and testimonials: honest-opinion requirement, material-connection disclosure, generally-achievable results
endorsement_or_testimonial.note: 16 CFR 255.0 (definitions), 255.1 (advertiser liability/monitoring), 255.5 (material connections). FTC guides interpreting Section 5 — doctrine formalized as guidance, not standalone statute.
endorsement_or_testimonial.definition: A span presenting a third party's opinion, experience, or results with the product: quoted customers, influencer statements, star ratings presented as user sentiment. The advertiser's own first-person marketing voice is not an endorsement; a named or implied outside voice is.

positive: "ClearPath cut my monthly payments in half!" — Jessica M.
@moneywithmarcus says this is the card to beat

negative.span: We think you'll love our simple application
negative.reason: advertiser's own voice — no third-party endorser
a media-placement claim, not a third party endorsing the product (general_udaap_representation if implying endorsement)

normalized_fields.endorser_named: boolean — an identifiable person/handle is attached
normalized_fields.material_connection_disclosed: boolean — compensation/relationship disclosure present in the same span or immediately adjacent
normalized_fields.atypical_result_claimed: boolean — a specific outcome (savings, rewards, score change) is asserted
normalized_fields.result_claim_text?: string — the asserted outcome, verbatim, if any

government_affiliation.legal_concept: Representations of government provision, endorsement, or affiliation in mortgage marketing
government_affiliation.note: Reg N 12 CFR 1014.3(n). Outside mortgage, government-affiliation implications fall to general deception doctrine.
government_affiliation.definition: A span invoking a government agency, program, or official status in connection with the product: FHA/VA/HUD references, 'government-backed', official-notice framing. Includes truthful program references (they still require verification) and implied affiliation through trade dress or 'official' vocabulary.

positive: FHA loans with as little as 3.5% down
Official notice: your property qualifies for a government refinance program
Backed by the full faith of federal programs

negative.span: We comply with all federal lending regulations
negative.reason: a compliance statement, not a claim of government provision, endorsement, or affiliation
a mandated licensing identifier, not an affiliation claim (it is a Disclosure, not a Claim)

normalized_fields.agency_or_program?: string — the named agency/program (FHA, VA, HUD, ...), if any
normalized_fields.is_program_reference: boolean — true when referencing a real loan program (FHA/VA product)
normalized_fields.affiliation_implied: boolean — true when the framing implies the sender IS or REPRESENTS a government entity ('official notice')

general_udaap_representation.legal_concept: Residual category: any other representation reachable as a deceptive act or practice — urgency devices, comparative/superlative claims, amount-offered claims, savings claims, soft-pull claims, debt-elimination claims
general_udaap_representation.note: No statutory definition by design — FTC Act Section 5 and CFPA Section 1031 supply the standard (misleads or likely to mislead; reasonable interpretation; material). Urgency and comparison claims specifically have no statutory test; their treatment is deception doctrine. Amount-offered claims ('up to $50,000') live here because a bare amount is not a Reg Z triggering term per interp-24, yet still needs truthfulness reconciliation.
general_udaap_representation.definition: The residual type for material representations governed only by the general deception standard. The extractor sets representation_kind to the closest sub-kind: urgency devices, measurable comparative/superlative claims, amount-offered claims, savings/outcome claims, soft-pull (credit-score-impact) claims, debt-elimination claims, geographic-availability claims. Non-material puffery ('great service') yields no claim at all.

positive: Checking your rate won't affect your credit score

negative.span: Friendly service from a team that cares
negative.reason: non-material puffery — no reasonable consumer takes it as a measurable claim; emit no claim
governed by a specific legal regime (promotional_or_introductory + rate_or_apr), not the residual

normalized_fields.representation_kind: enum: urgency_device | comparative_superlative | amount_offered | savings_claim | soft_pull_claim | debt_elimination | geographic_availability | other
normalized_fields.amount_value?: number — the offered amount, when representation_kind=amount_offered (serves PL-TRUTH-001 amount reconciliation)
normalized_fields.claimed_deadline?: string — the stated/implied expiry, when representation_kind=urgency_device (serves XP-URG-004)
normalized_fields.comparative_is_measurable?: boolean — superlative asserts a verifiable market fact, when representation_kind=comparative_superlative
